# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

    "description": "## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

- `browser_ext/` — Chrome MV3 extension pairing fa with the browser
  (issue #23): `sw/main.js` (entry, pairing storage, panel API,
  optional embedded-agent boot), `sw/bridge.js` (wire protocol v1
  client), `sw/ops.js` (browserReq op table), `sw/tabs.js` (task tab
  groups), `sw/cdp.js` (chrome.debugger trusted path), `sw/agent.js`
  (dart2js build artifact, gitignored, absent → bridge-only scaffold),
  `content/content.js` (isolated-world DOM ops), `panel/` (side panel).
  `dart/` is the `fa_browser_agent` package (path dep) compiled into
  `sw/agent.js` by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` — agent host,
  chrome.storage ExecutionEnv, provider streams (incl. deterministic
  `fake:` provider), DAP hub client. Tests: `browser_ext/dart/test`,
  `browser_ext/test` (node --test), `test/browser_ext/` (headless
  Chrome, integration tag). Docs: docs/browser-extension.md.
- `lib/src/browser/` — pure-Dart browser half: `bridge_protocol.dart`
  (wire protocol v1 — frame codec, ops/error codes, one-time
  `pairingToken()`, `browser-ext/` mailbox ids, reconnect backoff, mail
  dedupe) and `browser_tools.dart` (the eleven exec-tier `browser_*`
  tools over the injectable `BrowserController`; failures throw
  `BrowserToolException` carrying the wire code). Availability family
  `browser` + `browser_eval` in `agent_cli_tools.dart`
  (docs/tool-availability.md); CLI surface in
  `lib/src/cli/browser_bridge_commands.dart` (`/browser connect|status`).
- `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — `fa serve --bridge [--port N] [--token T]`
  loopback WebSocket bridge (binds 127.0.0.1 only, AC15; non-
  `chrome-extension://` origins refused): one-time token pairing
  (`.fah/bridge/token`, 0600, minted fresh per `/browser connect`),
  two-way mail relay over the messaging fabric, ping/pong keepalive,
  `browserReq`/`browserRes` correlation for the `browser_*` tools. The
  CLI mounts the same server in-process via `bin/fah.dart`'s
  `_FaBrowserBridgeHandle` (also the `BrowserController` seam).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.

So this is a story-development task: implement the goal — one app-storage namespace with a shared resolution helper, bootability checks, honest failures, id validation, tests.

Let me now explore the current state of the code more deeply to design the implementation:

1. **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host. Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.

Currently: `AppsStore` hardcodes `'apps'`, `'apps/$id/manifest.json'` everywhere; `JsAppInfo.dir => 'apps/$id'`; `_AppWidgetFileReader` maps paths under `dir`. There's no shared helper — literal string concatenation in many places. The fix: introduce a shared resolution helper, e.g. `AppStoragePaths` / `AppStorage` facade, used by both `AppsStore` and `JsAppEngine` (via `_AppWidgetFileReader`).

2. **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw StateError.

Currently `listApps` skips apps whose manifest.json fails to read (`raw == null → continue` — "half-created folder — healer's domain"). And a manifest that parses but whose widget.js is missing still shows a normal tile → tap → StateError. Fix: at list time, check bootability (manifest + entry file readable); if missing → `JsAppInfo.error` state (or a distinct "stored files missing" error) that names the storage root and missing paths. Note `JsAppInfo` already has an `error` field that renders an error badge on the tile.

3. **I3 (honest failure):** error names the storage root and exact missing paths. So when boot fails, the error message should say the root (e.g. `apps/2048/`) and the missing paths (manifest.json, widget.js).

4. **AC4:** traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) rejected at list and read. The shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root.

{
  "key": "gh-1614",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')",
    "description": "## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Chrome extension: opening "2048 Мини 🎲" fails — `Bad state: app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js` (thrown from `JsAppEngine` when manifest/entry unreadable via the ExecutionEnv). Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.
</details>"
  }
}

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/` — JS apps platform on `package:js_widget_runtime`
  (`^0.4.156` hosted — ships `jsr.openUrl` + the `webView` node and, since
  0.4.156 = upstream 9d57570 (gh-1341), the flutter_js bridge registers
  EVERY `__jsr_*` channel (`JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` is the source
  of truth), so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang forever on JSC
  builds; the git pin convention is drop-the-override-once-hosted-lands;
  `js_app_engine.dart` wires `openUrlHandler` over `url_launcher`
  (LaunchMode.externalApplication, {'__error': ...} rejections) and passes a
  `JsWebViewHost` (fa_webview_host.dart, `flutter_inappwebview` over the
  system default data store — never incognito; iOS/Android/macOS only, other
  platforms get the renderer placeholder via `createFaWebViewHost`) to BOTH
  the JsRuntimeConfig and the JsonWidgetRenderer in js_app_view.dart —
  flutter_inappwebview rides the coherent 6.2.0-beta.3 set because 6.1.x's
  android impl evaluates getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android.txt'),
  which AGP 9 removed (APK CI leg); the beta macos impl declares a 10.14
  floor while its Swift needs 10.15 (fails on both the SwiftPM and
  CocoaPods paths), so it is vendored with only the floor raised to the
  app's 14.0 (vendor/flutter_inappwebview_macos, pubspec override); return
  to ^6.1.x once 6.2.0 stable ships —
  earlier hosted line shipped the queued-callEvent-after-dispose guard +
  restart-safe bridge channels that the old git pin carried, plus the M3
  nodes/overlays/flChart/pickers/drawer catalog and M3 motion tokens; the
  use-after-free SIGSEGV is owned by `js_app_engine.dart`'s process-wide
  lifecycle serialization — releases must stay immediate, never deferred;
  the `map` node: center/zoom/markers/polylines/
  fitBounds, onTap/onMarkerTap). `flutter_js` itself is overridden in
  `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` to IstiN/flutter_js@74a11bf
  (fix-jscore-multi-instance: the shared native sendMessage callback routed
  to the LAST created runtime, so coexisting engines converted each other's
  JSValues with the wrong JSContext — SIGSEGV in JSC::JSLock::lock; the fork
  routes by executing context and refuses post-dispose evaluate): apps live in env-shared `apps/<id>/
  {manifest.json, widget.js}`; permissions in `apps_permissions.json` (network/
  allowedCommands/llm/homekit/health/contacts/calendar/microphone/
  notifications/media/keys/theme — default denied);
  `jsr.fa.*` bridge over exec (`fa.llm`, `fa.calendar`, `fa.home.*`,
  `fa.health.*`, `fa.asr.*`, `fa.notify.*`, `fa.theme` — declarative-only
  list/current/apply over installed theme packs, consent dialog per apply,
  no install/delete surface (issue #169); `fa.keys` — list/get/request the
  host's merged secrets (AgentService.hostSecrets); `request` renders the
  shared secret_request sheet from JsAppView and persists via
  AgentService.acceptSecretGrant; contacts is a gated "not
  available yet" stub); the `js-apps` skill is a package builtin
  (gh-1164 retired the `.fah/skills/` seeder — it is compiled into
  `builtinSkillFiles` by `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`, and the gh-1275
  packaging-content gate is `scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart`, wired
  into the app build workflows). Bundled demos (seeded by
  `AppsStore.demoAppIds`, assets in `flutter_app/assets/apps/` — each id
  MUST also have its `- assets/apps/<id>/` entry in pubspec.yaml, gated by
  `test/apps/demo_assets_declared_test.dart`): calculator,
  weather, stocks, crypto, animation-showcase, yolo-hello, calendar
  (`jsr.fa.calendar`), map (`map` node), health + homekit (real bridge on
  iOS, honest demo-panel fallback elsewhere), fitness-trainer — guided
  workout with a 3D animated coach (a realistic human baked from NAVER's
  anny body model — Apache-2.0 — into
  `assets/apps/fitness-trainer/models/coach_anny.glb` with 10
  hand-authored skeletal clips; baker script in
  `references/anny/tools/bake_coach_glb.py` — anny `local-bone` deltas in
  world axes → glTF: IBMs are column-major, mesh split into ≤16-joint
  surfaces for flame_3d, and the skinned node must NOT be parented to a
  joint (flame_3d's dependency count then never settles); rendered via
  the `scene3d` node + flame_3d; START-driven exercise/rest steps with
  per-clip mapping, pause/skip/quit, sessions persisted via jsr.storage;
  `integration_test/fitness_coach_screenshot_test.dart` screenshot-verifies
  it on the macOS host), english-teacher — the "Language Tutor": Duolingo-style
  quiz sessions (hearts/XP/streak, choice + typing modes), a per-language
  offline word bank (en/de/es/fr/pl picker persisted via jsr.storage),
  LLM-generated extra words via `jsr.fa.llm.chat` (manifest `llm: true`),
  3d-game (`scene3d` node +
  `jsr.scene3d.*` bridge on the runtime's flutter_cube/flame_3d dispatcher
  — the engine's `JsRuntimeConfig` and both renderers (JsAppView,
  AppTileHost) wire `js3dHost: createJs3dHost()`, tap picking flows back
  via `dispatchHostEvent('scene3d.tap:<id>')`). Demo seeding is

  last seeded — a file whose content no longer matches is user/agent-owned

  version, `storage.json` untouched). A demo id whose seeding FAILS

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.

- `browser_ext/` — Chrome MV3 extension pairing fa with the browser
  (issue #23): `sw/main.js` (entry, pairing storage, panel API,
  optional embedded-agent boot), `sw/bridge.js` (wire protocol v1
  client), `sw/ops.js` (browserReq op table), `sw/tabs.js` (task tab
  groups), `sw/cdp.js` (chrome.debugger trusted path), `sw/agent.js`
  (dart2js build artifact, gitignored, absent → bridge-only scaffold),
  `content/content.js` (isolated-world DOM ops), `panel/` (side panel).
  `dart/` is the `fa_browser_agent` package (path dep) compiled into
  `sw/agent.js` by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` — agent host,
  chrome.storage ExecutionEnv, provider streams (incl. deterministic
  `fake:` provider), DAP hub client. Tests: `browser_ext/dart/test`,
  `browser_ext/test` (node --test), `test/browser_ext/` (headless
  Chrome, integration tag). Docs: docs/browser-extension.md.
- `lib/src/browser/` — pure-Dart browser half: `bridge_protocol.dart`
  (wire protocol v1 — frame codec, ops/error codes, one-time
  `pairingToken()`, `browser-ext/` mailbox ids, reconnect backoff, mail
  dedupe) and `browser_tools.dart` (the eleven exec-tier `browser_*`
  tools over the injectable `BrowserController`; failures throw
  `BrowserToolException` carrying the wire code). Availability family
  `browser` + `browser_eval` in `agent_cli_tools.dart`
  (docs/tool-availability.md); CLI surface in
  `lib/src/cli/browser_bridge_commands.dart` (`/browser connect|status`).
- `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — `fa serve --bridge [--port N] [--token T]`
  loopback WebSocket bridge (binds 127.0.0.1 only, AC15; non-
  `chrome-extension://` origins refused): one-time token pairing
  (`.fah/bridge/token`, 0600, minted fresh per `/browser connect`),
  two-way mail relay over the messaging fabric, ping/pong keepalive,
  `browserReq`/`browserRes` correlation for the `browser_*` tools. The
  CLI mounts the same server in-process via `bin/fah.dart`'s
  `_FaBrowserBridgeHandle` (also the `BrowserController` seam).

## Hard architecture rules

  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network

    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.

So this is a story-development task: implement the goal — one app-storage namespace with a shared resolution helper, bootability checks, honest failures, id validation, tests.

Let me now explore the current state of the code more deeply to design the implementation:

1. **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host. Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.

Currently: `AppsStore` hardcodes `'apps'`, `'apps/$id/manifest.json'` everywhere; `JsAppInfo.dir => 'apps/$id'`; `_AppWidgetFileReader` maps paths under `dir`. There's no shared helper — literal string concatenation in many places. The fix: introduce a shared resolution helper, e.g. `AppStoragePaths` / `AppStorage` facade, used by both `AppsStore` and `JsAppEngine` (via `_AppWidgetFileReader`).

2. **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw StateError.

Currently `listApps` skips apps whose manifest.json fails to read (`raw == null → continue` — "half-created folder — healer's domain"). And a manifest that parses but whose widget.js is missing still shows a normal tile → tap → StateError. Fix: at list time, check bootability (manifest + entry file readable); if missing → `JsAppInfo.error` state (or a distinct "stored files missing" error) that names the storage root and missing paths. Note `JsAppInfo` already has an `error` field that renders an error badge on the tile.

3. **I3 (honest failure):** error names the storage root and exact missing paths. So when boot fails, the error message should say the root (e.g. `apps/2048/`) and the missing paths (manifest.json, widget.js).

4. **AC4:** traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) rejected at list and read. The shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root.

Wait — but current app ids include things like `2048-mini`? Let me check what ids exist in the catalog and existing tests. The regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` allows lowercase alnum and dashes, length 2–32. But existing apps might have underscores or digits-only ids... e.g. `2048` — starts with digit `2`, then `048` — `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` matches `2048`. OK.

But wait — do catalog app ids always match this? Let me check the catalog service and any id validation. Also `AppsStore` skips ids starting with '.' (`.demo_seeds.json`, `.installed.json`).

Let me look at how apps get created (catalog_service.dart install path) to see id formats.

Also **the "read side"**: `_AppWidgetFileReader` maps `'$dir/widget.js' → '$dir/$entryFile'`. `WidgetManifest.fromStorage(dir, reader: reader)` — that's from package:js_widget_runtime. Let me check that package's API.

- `browser_ext/` — Chrome MV3 extension pairing fa with the browser
  (issue #23): `sw/main.js` (entry, pairing storage, panel API,
  optional embedded-agent boot), `sw/bridge.js` (wire protocol v1
  client), `sw/ops.js` (browserReq op table), `sw/tabs.js` (task tab
  groups), `sw/cdp.js` (chrome.debugger trusted path), `sw/agent.js`
  (dart2js build artifact, gitignored, absent → bridge-only scaffold),
  `content/content.js` (isolated-world DOM ops), `panel/` (side panel).
  `dart/` is the `fa_browser_agent` package (path dep) compiled into
  `sw/agent.js` by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` — agent host,
  chrome.storage ExecutionEnv, provider streams (incl. deterministic
  `fake:` provider), DAP hub client. Tests: `browser_ext/dart/test`,
  `browser_ext/test` (node --test), `test/browser_ext/` (headless
  Chrome, integration tag). Docs: docs/browser-extension.md.
- `lib/src/browser/` — pure-Dart browser half: `bridge_protocol.dart`
  (wire protocol v1 — frame codec, ops/error codes, one-time
  `pairingToken()`, `browser-ext/` mailbox ids, reconnect backoff, mail
  dedupe) and `browser_tools.dart` (the eleven exec-tier `browser_*`
  tools over the injectable `BrowserController`; failures throw
  `BrowserToolException` carrying the wire code). Availability family
  `browser` + `browser_eval` in `agent_cli_tools.dart`
  (docs/tool-availability.md); CLI surface in
  `lib/src/cli/browser_bridge_commands.dart` (`/browser connect|status`).
- `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — `fa serve --bridge [--port N] [--token T]`
  loopback WebSocket bridge (binds 127.0.0.1 only, AC15; non-
  `chrome-extension://` origins refused): one-time token pairing
  (`.fah/bridge/token`, 0600, minted fresh per `/browser connect`),
  two-way mail relay over the messaging fabric, ping/pong keepalive,
  `browserReq`/`browserRes` correlation for the `browser_*` tools. The
  CLI mounts the same server in-process via `bin/fah.dart`'s
  `_FaBrowserBridgeHandle` (also the `BrowserController` seam).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.

So this is a story-development task: implement the goal — one app-storage namespace with a shared resolution helper, bootability checks, honest failures, id validation, tests.

Let me now explore the current state of the code more deeply to design the implementation:

1. **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host. Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.

Currently: `AppsStore` hardcodes `'apps'`, `'apps/$id/manifest.json'` everywhere; `JsAppInfo.dir => 'apps/$id'`; `_AppWidgetFileReader` maps paths under `dir`. There's no shared helper — literal string concatenation in many places. The fix: introduce a shared resolution helper, e.g. `AppStoragePaths` / `AppStorage` facade, used by both `AppsStore` and `JsAppEngine` (via `_AppWidgetFileReader`).

2. **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw StateError.

Currently `listApps` skips apps whose manifest.json fails to read (`raw == null → continue` — "half-created folder — healer's domain"). And a manifest that parses but whose widget.js is missing still shows a normal tile → tap → StateError. So this is a story-development task: implement the goal — one app-storage namespace with a shared resolution helper, bootability checks, honest failures, id validation, tests.

Let me now explore the current state of the code more deeply to design the implementation:

1. **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host. Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.

Currently: `AppsStore` hardcodes `'apps'`, `'apps/$id/manifest.json'` everywhere; `JsAppInfo.dir => 'apps/$id'`; `_AppWidgetFileReader` maps paths under `dir`. There's no shared helper — literal string concatenation in many places. The fix: introduce a shared resolution helper, e.g. `AppStoragePaths` / `AppStorage` facade, used by both `AppsStore` and `JsAppEngine` (via `_AppWidgetFileReader`).

2. **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw StateError.

Currently `listApps` skips apps whose manifest.json fails to read (`raw == null → continue` — "half-created folder — healer's domain"). And a manifest that parses but whose widget.js is missing still shows a normal tile → tap → StateError. Fix: at list time, check bootability (manifest + entry file readable); if missing → `JsAppInfo.error` state (or a distinct "stored files missing" error) that names the storage root and missing paths. Note `JsAppInfo` already has an `error` field that renders an error badge on the tile.

3. **I3 (honest failure):** error names the storage root and exact missing paths. So when boot fails, the error message should say the root (e.g. `apps/2048/`) and the missing paths (manifest.json, widget.js).

4. **AC4:** traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) rejected at list and read. The shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root.

So this is a story-development task: implement the goal — one app-storage namespace with a shared resolution helper, bootability checks, honest failures, id validation, tests.

Let me now explore the current state of the code more deeply to design the implementation:

1. **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host. Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.

Currently: `AppsStore` hardcodes `'apps'`, `'apps/$id/manifest.json'` everywhere; `JsAppInfo.dir => 'apps/$id'`; `_AppWidgetFileReader` maps paths under `dir`. There's no shared helper — literal string concatenation in many places. The fix: introduce a shared resolution helper, e.g. `AppStoragePaths` / `AppStorage` facade, used by both `AppsStore` and `JsAppEngine` (via `_AppWidgetFileReader`).

2. **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw StateError.

Currently `listApps` skips apps whose manifest.json fails to read (`raw == null → continue` — "half-created folder — healer's domain"). And a manifest that parses but whose widget.js is missing still shows a normal tile → tap → StateError. Fix: at list time, check bootability (manifest + entry file readable); if missing → `JsAppInfo.error` state (or a distinct "stored files missing" error) that names the storage root and missing paths. Note `JsAppInfo` already has an `error` field that renders an error badge on the tile.

3. **I3 (honest failure):** error names the storage root and exact missing paths. So when boot fails, the error message should say the root (e.g. `apps/2048/`) and the missing paths (manifest.json, widget.js).

4. **AC4:** traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) rejected at list and read. The shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root.

Now — the TDD workflow. Let me write tests FIRST (RED), then implementation (GREEN).

Test plan:

**File 1: `flutter_app/test/apps/app_storage_test.dart`** (UT — root-resolution helper):
- id validation table: valid (`2048`, `a`, `ab`, `my-app`, `a0`), invalid (``, `A` (uppercase), `a_b`, `../x`, `..`, `.`, `a/b`, `/abs`, `C:\\x`? (backslash), ` leading space`? (space fails pattern), 33-char (too long), `-abc` (starts with dash — pattern says first char `[a-z0-9]` → invalid), unicode `прил`).
- `appDir` returns `apps/<id>` for valid; throws for invalid with message naming the id + rule.
- `appFile` joins and validates name segments (`game/first.js` ok; `../x.js` throws; `/abs.js` throws; `` throws; `a\\b` throws).
- `manifestPath`/`entryPath` shapes.
- VM/web parity: the helper is pure Dart — assert the SAME outputs across... hmm "parity table" — the honest test: resolution does not depend on `Platform`/`kIsWeb` (there's no branch), pin the exact path strings. I'll write it as a table of (id, expected path) and assert identical results — plus assert no `dart:io`-dependent behavior (trivially true). Keep it simple: a table test.

**File 2: additions to `flutter_app/test/apps_store_test.dart`** (list-side, I2/I3 + AC3 + AC4-list):
- REG (AC3 divergence): env with `apps/2048/manifest.json` (parses) but NO widget.js → `listApps` returns the app WITH a non-null `error` containing `apps/2048/widget.js` and the root `apps/2048/`; a second healthy app still lists clean.

- missing-dir case: `apps/ghost/` dir exists but empty → manifest read null → skipped (not listed — 'list no longer shows it').  Wait — empty dir: `listDir('apps')` returns the dir entry; manifest read null → skip. Good.
- AC4-list: hostile dirs `apps/..` (can't exist in a real fs, but the memory env — actually MemoryExecutionEnv listDir returns real dirs; a dir named `..` can't be created via writeFile... I can test via a fake env that returns hostile entries). Simplest: a thin fake ExecutionEnv wrapping memory that injects hostile listing entries. Hmm — worth it? The store's guard `AppStorage.isValidId(id) → skip` needs a hostile name to flow through. A FakeEnv returning `FileInfo(path: 'apps/../evil', kind: directory, name: '../evil')` — let me check FileInfo's shape: `name` field exists (used by store: `entry.name`). I'll write a small `_HostileListEnv` implements ExecutionEnv delegating to a MemoryExecutionEnv but overriding listDir to append hostile entries. That's ~40 lines. Worth it for AC4.
- Multi-item case (R5 rule: 2+ items): craft three apps — healthy, entry-missing, manifest-missing — assert each distinct outcome in one scan.

**File 3: additions to `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart`** (read-side, I3 + AC4-read + AC1):
- missing entry (manifest present) → StateError message contains `app entry not found`, the root `apps/demo/`, and the exact missing path `apps/demo/widget.js` (distinct message 1).
- missing manifest (widget.js present) → boots via fromStorage defaults?? Wait — `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` only needs widget.js to exist; manifest missing → derived defaults → boot SUCCEEDS. So missing-manifest is NOT a boot failure — it's the list-side skip. Hmm! The ticket's IT says "missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages". For the ENGINE: missing-manifest → fromStorage succeeds with defaults (that's the upstream behavior — boot works). So the three distinct cases at the ENGINE level:
  - entry (widget.js) missing entirely → 'app entry not found … missing: apps/<id>/widget.js'.
  - whole dir missing → 'app entry not found … missing: apps/<id>/manifest.json, apps/<id>/widget.js' (both missing) — or if manifest also absent → both listed.
  - manifest.json present but entry unreadable?? exists()==true but read returns null — memory env can't produce that... The reader clamp could: a manifest `files: ['../../x.js']`... no, readJs with files list doesn't return null (missing parts → comment). readJs returns null only when `files` empty and mainJsPath read null — i.e., exists said true but read null (torn/race). Can't fabricate with MemoryExecutionEnv directly — skip; the message branch is still unit-testable? The two branches (manifest==null vs js==null) produce different messages; I can test the manifest==null one. For the js==null branch — hmm, construct a fake WidgetFileReader? `assembleEntryJsForTest` takes env, not reader. Fine: message differences between "dir missing entirely" (both files listed) and "only entry missing" (only entry listed) give the distinct-messages requirement. Plus missing-manifest (defaults boot) is distinct behavior. Good enough — honest and testable.
- AC4-read: `AppStorage.appDir('../evil')` throws; the reader: `reader.readString('apps/demo/../../secrets.json')` → null; `reader.exists('/etc/passwd')` → false; and the underlying env NEVER got the read (guard with a recording env or just assert null + that `env.exists` of the escaped path was never called — simpler: write a sentinel file OUTSIDE the app dir, assert its content is not returned).

- AC1 IT: engine `start()` on MemoryExecutionEnv with `apps/2048/` present+complete → boots (same entry-assembly path) — existing tests cover engine boot with apps/demo; add a 2048-shaped one? The "same entry-assembly path" is by construction (start calls _assembleEntryJs). The IT: listed-but-missing → no StateError LEAK: the leak surface is the view (catches into error card) and the store (error state). For the engine start, the StateError is still thrown (start fails honestly) — the "no StateError leak" in AC1 refers to the app experience: the listed app renders the explicit state instead of tapping into a crash. Covered by store tests + the improved message.

expect(AppStorage.manifestPath(id), JsAppInfo(...).manifestPath);
expect(reader.exists(AppStorage.entryPath(id)), env.exists(...)) — equivalence
```
Concretely: craft `apps/x/` with manifest only; reader.exists('apps/x/widget.js') == false AND the store's bootability probe reports missing — both go through `AppStorage.entryPath`. I'll pin: `AppStorage.entryPath(id) == '${AppStorage.appDir(id)}/widget.js'` and that `_AppWidgetFileReader.exists(that exact path)` matches the env — via the public seam `appWidgetFileReaderForTest`. Good.

Now about **`JsAppInfo.dir` with invalid ids**: `fromManifest` fallbackId comes from the dir name (already validated at list). But `JsAppInfo` can be constructed directly with any id (tests do `JsAppInfo.fromManifest({'id': 'demo'})`). If `dir` routes through `AppStorage.appDir(id)` it would THROW for weird ids (e.g. 'demo' is fine; 'My Widget' throws). Where do weird ids come from? `dirOverride` path is separate. A manifest `id` field can be anything — `JsAppInfo.fromManifest` uses `(json['id'] ?? fallbackId)`. The engine boots `app.dir`. If a manifest declares `id: "../../x"`, today `dir` = 'apps/../../x' → reads escape! That's EXACTLY the AC4 threat. With validation: `dir` throws ArgumentError → the view catches (start error card) — honest rejection at read. And the LIST: `JsAppInfo.fromManifest` with hostile manifest id → the store should sanitize: use the DIRECTORY name (validated) as the id, not the manifest-declared id... wait — today's behavior: `id: (json['id'] ?? fallbackId)` — the manifest id wins; the tile then reads `apps/<manifest-id>/` — if manifest id != dir name, reads MISS (another listed-unreadable vector!). OK. Catalog ids come from the hosted `fa_widgets` catalog. Ids like `2048` are the norm. The regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is the ticket's rule.

Now the key design decision — where does the "one resolved root" actually live, and what concretely changes:

### Current state (paths spread as literals):
- `AppsStore`: `'apps'` literal in listDir; `'apps/$id/manifest.json'` reads; `'apps/.demo_seeds.json'`, `'apps/.installed.json'`, `'apps/.catalog_cache_v2.json'`; `JsAppInfo.dir => 'apps/$id'`.
- `JsAppEngine._assembleEntryJs`: `_AppWidgetFileReader(env, dir: app.dir, entryFile)` → throws `StateError('app entry not found: $dir/$entryFile')`.
- `_AppWidgetFileReader._map`: redirects `$dir/widget.js` → `$dir/$entryFile`.

### The implementation plan (TDD):

**1. `flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`** — `AppStorage`:
- `static const root = 'apps'`
- `static bool isValidId(String id)` — `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`

The catalog download path validates ids loosely (`unsafe()` check). Real catalog ids are like `2048`, `todo`, etc. Let me check the actual catalog to be safe: is there a catalog in the repo? Let me check `catalog_service.dart` for base URL and maybe a local copy. Also check `test/apps/fixtures`.

Actually — I should decide the id validation carefully. The ticket's security section says: "I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root". This is 2–32 chars, lowercase alnum + dash.

Now, what about list: an id that fails validation (e.g. a directory named `My App` or `..` or `x.y`) — should the listing hide it or show the missing-files state? Per AC4: "traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read". The safest: at LIST, invalid-id directories are skipped (not listed — they can never be started through the shared resolver). At READ, an invalid id throws an ArgumentError naming the id and the rule (never a StateError 'app entry not found').

But hold on — would that break existing apps with ids not matching the pattern? Let me check the actual widget catalog ids used in tests, and the demo ids (empty now). Let me search the repo for the actual hosted catalog JSON. `catalog_service.dart` base URL:
{"command":"sed -n 1,120p flutter_app/lib/apps/catalog_service.dart"}

OK. Catalog ids come from the hosted `fa_widgets` catalog. Ids like `2048` are the norm. The regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is the ticket's rule.

Now the key design decision — where does the "one resolved root" actually live, and what concretely changes:

### Current state (paths spread as literals):
- `AppsStore`: `'apps'` literal in listDir; `'apps/$id/manifest.json'` reads; `'apps/.demo_seeds.json'`, `'apps/.installed.json'`, `'apps/.catalog_cache_v2.json'`; `JsAppInfo.dir => 'apps/$id'`.
- `JsAppEngine._assembleEntryJs`: `_AppWidgetFileReader(env, dir: app.dir, entryFile)` → throws `StateError('app entry not found: $dir/$entryFile')`.
- `_AppWidgetFileReader._map`: redirects `$dir/widget.js` → `$dir/$entryFile`.

### The implementation plan (TDD):

**1. `flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`** — `AppStorage`:
- `static const root = 'apps'`
- `static bool isValidId(String id)` — `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`
- `static String appDir(String id)` — validates, returns `apps/<id>`; invalid → `ArgumentError` (or a dedicated `AppStoragePathError`) naming the id + rule.
- `static String appFile(String id, String name)` — validates the file name too (no `/`, `\`, `..`, not empty, not absolute; a simple safe-segment check).
- `static String manifestPath(String id)` → `apps/<id>/manifest.json`
- `static String entryPath(String id, {String entry = 'widget.js'})`
- Maybe `static String? tryAppDir(String id)` returning null for invalid ids (used by the listing to skip hostile/invalid dirs).

Wait — should the dir join be done via `env.joinPath`? That'd be an async round trip per call; the existing code just uses forward-slash string joins everywhere (web + VM). Keep it synchronous and pure: 'apps/<id>/<name>'.

**2. `AppsStore.listApps`** — resolve through `AppStorage`:
- `final listing = await _env.listDir(AppStorage.root);`
- For each dir entry: validate id — invalid (traversal/absolute/dot) → skip (never listed — AC4 "rejected at list"; a `../x` entry can never start).
- Then bootability check (I2): manifest readable AND entry (widget.js or tile entry? — the boot entry is widget.js; the tile entry is the tile's) ... 

Careful: I2 says "anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit 'stored files missing' state with the root that was searched". The Apps tab lists full apps (entry = widget.js). The entry readability check must mirror the boot path exactly: `_AppWidgetFileReader.exists('$dir/widget.js')` — actually the boot path checks `reader.exists('$dir/widget.js')` (via `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`) and then reads. The honest approach: check `manifest.json` readable + `widget.js` exists. Missing → `JsAppInfo(error: 'stored files missing under apps/<id>: manifest.json', ...)` or similar.

Wait, but the current list code SKIPS apps whose manifest read returns null ("half-created folder — healer's domain"). Per AC3: "a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state)". So the divergence regression wants: list no longer shows unstartable apps OR shows the missing-files state. Since with a single root there's no "read root doesn't see it" scenario anymore, the residual case is "listed dir exists but files missing/incomplete" — the healer's half-created folder. Keeping the current skip for missing manifest (healer's domain) is consistent with "list no longer shows it". But for a manifest that EXISTS and parses, yet widget.js is missing — today it lists a tile that StateErrors on tap. That's the I2 violation to fix: show the explicit missing-files state.

Hmm — but what about the seed/healer? Let me check: is there a healer that removes half-created folders? `apps/.demo_seeds.json` reseeds broken demo manifests. The "healer" comment — let me grep for it.

The catalog download path validates ids loosely (`unsafe()` check). Real catalog ids are like `2048`, `todo`, etc. Let me check the actual catalog to be safe: is there a catalog in the repo? Let me check `catalog_service.dart` for base URL and maybe a local copy. Also check `test/apps/fixtures`.

Actually — I should decide the id validation carefully. The ticket's security section says: "I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root". This is 2–32 chars, lowercase alnum + dash.

Now, what about list: an id that fails validation (e.g. a directory named `My App` or `..` or `x.y`) — should the listing hide it or show the missing-files state? Per AC4: "traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read". The safest: at LIST, invalid-id directories are skipped (not listed — they can never be started through the shared resolver). At READ, an invalid id throws an ArgumentError naming the id and the rule (never a StateError 'app entry not found').

But hold on — would that break existing apps with ids not matching the pattern? Let me check the actual widget catalog ids used in tests, and the demo ids (empty now). Let me search the repo for the actual hosted catalog JSON. `catalog_service.dart` base URL:
{"command":"sed -n 1,120p flutter_app/lib/apps/catalog_service.dart"}

OK. Catalog ids come from the hosted `fa_widgets` catalog. Ids like `2048` are the norm. The regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is the ticket's rule.

Now the key design decision — where does the "one resolved root" actually live, and what concretely changes:

### Current state (paths spread as literals):
- `AppsStore`: `'apps'` literal in listDir; `'apps/$id/manifest.json'` reads; `'apps/.demo_seeds.json'`, `'apps/.installed.json'`, `'apps/.catalog_cache_v2.json'`; `JsAppInfo.dir => 'apps/$id'`.
- `JsAppEngine._assembleEntryJs`: `_AppWidgetFileReader(env, dir: app.dir, entryFile)` → throws `StateError('app entry not found: $dir/$entryFile')`.
- `_AppWidgetFileReader._map`: redirects `$dir/widget.js` → `$dir/$entryFile`.

### The implementation plan (TDD):

**1. `flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`** — `AppStorage`:
- `static const root = 'apps'`
- `static bool isValidId(String id)` — `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`

blocks.text:
shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.

On the web/extension, the IndexedDB snapshot persistence can persist mid-write: `apps/2048/manifest.json` restored but `apps/2048/widget.js` lost (or vice versa). Then the listing shows the tile (manifest parses), tap → `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` returns null (widget.js missing) → `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')`.

So the namespace divergence: the "legacy list root" vs "read root" in the ticket is one possible cause; the other is "the entry was never persisted" (mid-install torn snapshot). Both land as listed-but-unreadable. Our fix handles it at two layers:

1. **Single shared resolver (I1)**: `AppStorage` produces every path for list + read; the reader (`_AppWidgetFileReader`) resolves through it; `AppsStore` lists through it. Id validation + clamping (AC4).

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

Now the key design decision — where does the "one resolved root" actually live, and what concretely changes:

### Current state (paths spread as literals):
- `AppsStore`: `'apps'` literal in listDir; `'apps/$id/manifest.json'` reads; `'apps/.demo_seeds.json'`, `'apps/.installed.json'`, `'apps/.catalog_cache_v2.json'`; `JsAppInfo.dir => 'apps/$id'`.
- `JsAppEngine._assembleEntryJs`: `_AppWidgetFileReader(env, dir: app.dir, entryFile)` → throws `StateError('app entry not found: $dir/$entryFile')`.
- `_AppWidgetFileReader._map`: redirects `$dir/widget.js` → `$dir/$entryFile`.

### The implementation plan (TDD):

**1. `flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`** — `AppStorage`:
- `static const root = 'apps'`
- `static bool isValidId(String id)` — `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`
- `static String appDir(String id)` — validates, returns `apps/<id>`; invalid → `ArgumentError` (or a dedicated `AppStoragePathError`) naming the id + rule.
- `static String appFile(String id, String name)` — validates the file name too (no `/`, `\`, `..`, not empty, not absolute; a simple safe-segment check).
- `static String manifestPath(String id)` → `apps/<id>/manifest.json`
- `static String entryPath(String id, {String entry = 'widget.js'})`
- Maybe `static String? tryAppDir(String id)` returning null for invalid ids (used by the listing to skip hostile/invalid dirs).

Wait — should the dir join be done via `env.joinPath`? That'd be an async round trip per call; the existing code just uses forward-slash string joins everywhere (web + VM). Keep it synchronous and pure: 'apps/<id>/<name>'.

**2. `AppsStore.listApps`** — resolve through `AppStorage`:
- `final listing = await _env.listDir(AppStorage.root);`
- For each dir entry: validate id — invalid (traversal/absolute/dot) → skip (never listed — AC4 "rejected at list"; a `../x` entry can never start).
- Then bootability check (I2): manifest readable AND entry (widget.js or tile entry? — the boot entry is widget.js; the tile entry is the tile's) ... 

Careful: I2 says "anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit 'stored files missing' state with the root that was searched". The Apps tab lists full apps (entry = widget.js). The entry readability check must mirror the boot path exactly: `_AppWidgetFileReader.exists('$dir/widget.js')` — actually the boot path checks `reader.exists('$dir/widget.js')` (via `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`) and then reads. The honest approach: check `manifest.json` readable + `widget.js` exists. Missing → `JsAppInfo(error: 'stored files missing under apps/<id>: manifest.json', ...)` or similar.

Per AC3: "a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state)". So the divergence regression wants: list no longer shows unstartable apps OR shows the missing-files state. Since with a single root there's no "read root doesn't see it" scenario anymore, the residual case is "listed dir exists but files missing/incomplete" — the healer's half-created folder. Keeping the current skip for missing manifest (healer's domain) is consistent with "list no longer shows it". 3. **Honest failure at boot (I3)**: when the engine still fails to assemble (race: file deleted after list; or the view bypasses the store), the error names the storage root + the exact missing paths rather than a bare `app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js`. Now — the TDD workflow. Let me write tests FIRST (RED), then implementation (GREEN).

Test plan:

**File 1: `flutter_app/test/apps/app_storage_test.dart`** (UT — root-resolution helper):
- id validation table: valid (`2048`, `a`, `ab`, `my-app`, `a0`), invalid (``, `A` (uppercase), `a_b`, `../x`, `..`, `.`, `a/b`, `/abs`, `C:\\x`? (backslash), ` leading space`? (space fails pattern), 33-char (too long), `-abc` (starts with dash — pattern says first char `[a-z0-9]` → invalid), unicode `прил`).
- `appDir` returns `apps/<id>` for valid; throws for invalid with message naming the id + rule.
- `appFile` joins and validates name segments (`game/first.js` ok; `../x.js` throws; `/abs.js` throws; `` throws; `a\\b` throws).
- `manifestPath`/`entryPath` shapes.
- VM/web parity: the helper is pure Dart — assert the SAME outputs across... hmm "parity table" — the honest test: resolution does not depend on `Platform`/`kIsWeb` (there's no branch), pin the exact path strings. I'll write it as a table of (id, expected path) and assert identical results — plus assert no `dart:io`-dependent behavior (trivially true). Keep it simple: a table test.

**File 2: additions to `flutter_app/test/apps_store_test.dart`** (list-side, I2/I3 + AC3 + AC4-list):
- REG (AC3 divergence): env with `apps/2048/manifest.json` (parses) but NO widget.js → `listApps` returns the app WITH a non-null `error` containing `apps/2048/widget.js` and the root `apps/2048/`; a second healthy app still lists clean.
- present-and-startable: manifest + widget.js → no error.
- missing-dir case: `apps/ghost/` dir exists but empty → manifest read null → skipped (not listed — 'list no longer shows it').  Wait — empty dir: `listDir('apps')` returns the dir entry; manifest read null → skip. Good.
- AC4-list: hostile dirs `apps/..` (can't exist in a real fs, but the memory env — actually MemoryExecutionEnv listDir returns real dirs; a dir named `..` can't be created via writeFile... I can test via a fake env that returns hostile entries). Simplest: a thin fake ExecutionEnv wrapping memory that injects hostile listing entries. Hmm — worth it? The store's guard `AppStorage.isValidId(id) → skip` needs a hostile name to flow through. A FakeEnv returning `FileInfo(path: 'apps/../evil', kind: directory, name: '../evil')` — let me check FileInfo's shape: `name` field exists (used by store: `entry.name`). I'll write a small `_HostileListEnv` implements ExecutionEnv delegating to a MemoryExecutionEnv but overriding listDir to append hostile entries. That's ~40 lines. Worth it for AC4.
- Multi-item case (R5 rule: 2+ items): craft three apps — healthy, entry-missing, manifest-missing — assert each distinct outcome in one scan.

- missing manifest (widget.js present) → boots via fromStorage defaults?? Wait — `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` only needs widget.js to exist; manifest missing → derived defaults → boot SUCCEEDS. So missing-manifest is NOT a boot failure — it's the list-side skip. Hmm! The ticket's IT says "missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages". For the ENGINE: missing-manifest → fromStorage succeeds with defaults (that's the upstream behavior — boot works). So the three distinct cases at the ENGINE level:
  - entry (widget.js) missing entirely → 'app entry not found … missing: apps/<id>/widget.js'.
  - whole dir missing → 'app entry not found … missing: apps/<id>/manifest.json, apps/<id>/widget.js' (both missing) — or if manifest also absent → both listed.
  - manifest.json present but entry unreadable?? exists()==true but read returns null — memory env can't produce that... The reader clamp could: a manifest `files: ['../../x.js']`... no, readJs with files list doesn't return null (missing parts → comment). readJs returns null only when `files` empty and mainJsPath read null — i.e., exists said true but read null (torn/race). Can't fabricate with MemoryExecutionEnv directly — skip; the message branch is still unit-testable? The two branches (manifest==null vs js==null) produce different messages; I can test the manifest==null one. For the js==null branch — hmm, construct a fake WidgetFileReader? `assembleEntryJsForTest` takes env, not reader. Fine: message differences between "dir missing entirely" (both files listed) and "only entry missing" (only entry listed) give the distinct-messages requirement. Plus missing-manifest (defaults boot) is distinct behavior. Good enough — honest and testable.
- AC4-read: `AppStorage.appDir('../evil')` throws; the reader: `reader.readString('apps/demo/../../secrets.json')` → null; `reader.exists('/etc/passwd')` → false; and the underlying env NEVER got the read (guard with a recording env or just assert null + that `env.exists` of the escaped path was never called — simpler: write a sentinel file OUTSIDE the app dir, assert its content is not returned).

For the engine start, the StateError is still thrown (start fails honestly) — the "no StateError leak" in AC1 refers to the app experience: the listed app renders the explicit state instead of tapping into a crash. Covered by store tests + the improved message.

expect(AppStorage.entryPath(id), JsAppInfo(...).widgetPath);
expect(AppStorage.manifestPath(id), JsAppInfo(...).manifestPath);
expect(reader.exists(AppStorage.entryPath(id)), env.exists(...)) — equivalence

Concretely: craft `apps/x/` with manifest only; reader.exists('apps/x/widget.js') == false AND the store's bootability probe reports missing — both go through `AppStorage.entryPath`. I'll pin: `AppStorage.entryPath(id) == '${AppStorage.appDir(id)}/widget.js'` and that `_AppWidgetFileReader.exists(that exact path)` matches the env — via the public seam `appWidgetFileReaderForTest`. Good.

Now about **`JsAppInfo.dir` with invalid ids**: `fromManifest` fallbackId comes from the dir name (already validated at list). But `JsAppInfo` can be constructed directly with any id (tests do `JsAppInfo.fromManifest({'id': 'demo'})`). If `dir` routes through `AppStorage.appDir(id)` it would THROW for weird ids (e.g. 'demo' is fine; 'My Widget' throws). Where do weird ids come from? `dirOverride` path is separate. A manifest `id` field can be anything — `JsAppInfo.fromManifest` uses `(json['id'] ?? fallbackId)`. The engine boots `app.dir`. If a manifest declares `id: "../../x"`, today `dir` = 'apps/../../x' → reads escape! That's EXACTLY the AC4 threat. With validation: `dir` throws ArgumentError → the view catches (start error card) — honest rejection at read. And the LIST: `JsAppInfo.fromManifest` with hostile manifest id → the store should sanitize: use the DIRECTORY name (validated) as the id, not the manifest-declared id... wait — today's behavior: `id: (json['id'] ?? fallbackId)` — the manifest id wins; the tile then reads `apps/<manifest-id>/` — if manifest id != dir name, reads MISS (another listed-unreadable vector!). Hmm interesting: `apps/2048/manifest.json` declaring `"id": "2048-мини"` → tile resolves `apps/2048-мини/widget.js` → not found → StateEr…

shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.

        working-directory: flutter_app

          set -euo pipefail

          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
